title: Nightfall Brewery onramp — field notes
content:
Context:
- Quick capture from 2025-09-17 discovery call with Nightfall Brewery (edge-connected brewery chain; 12 locations, US-only for now). They want a private deployment of Redwood for a set of cashier/ops assistants and a recipe-generation feature tied to internal inventory signals.
- Primary ask: low-cost private inference (on prem for PII logs + some hosted fallback), predictable latency under 120ms p50 for short prompts (<=128 tokens), and auditability for recipe provenance.

Attendees:
- Nightfall: Jenna Ortiz (CTO), Malik Davenport (SRE), Clara Huang (Data Eng)
- Redwood: Priya Natarajan (SE), Marcus Lee (Infra), Sofia Alvarez (Privacy/Compliance)

High-level requirements captured:
1) Deployment mode: Private control plane with customer-managed VPC + optional on-prem edge nodes at 3 hub locations.
   - Must support offline/air-gap option for one location (brewery with intermittent connectivity).
2) SLA target: 99.5% uptime for dedicated model endpoints during business hours (08:00-20:00 local).
3) Latency: target p50 < 120ms for single-turn prompts (prompt+generation <=128 tokens). 95th percentile can be higher but prefer <400ms.
4) Cost: Need predictable monthly spend. They prefer reserved capacity pricing with burst enabled.
5) Data residency & audit: logs stored for 13 months, redaction pipeline for PII, ability to export full audit trail for a given request id. KMS integration (Azure Key Vault preferred).
6) Model and versions: start with a 7B open model quantized for INT8/4-bit. Want a plan to upgrade to larger model family if needed.

Technical notes / gotchas from the call:
- Network topology: sites are in three regional hubs behind NAT with limited inbound rules. They asked if Redwood can initiate outbound-only connections from edge nodes to control plane — yes but need to map persistent egress IPs for their firewall team.
- Air-gapped site: requires an on-prem install package + offline model artifact transfer process. Need checklist for checksum verification and instructions for manual KV cache warmup.
- KV cache hit patterns: their use-case has many short prefixes (menu items + inventory tokens). We should recommend prefix caching and per-customer cache namespace. Make sure eviction policy is documented.
- Latency sensitivity: some cashier flows will be integrated into POS with a hard timeout of 250ms. Recommend testing with 5ms network jitter emulation to mirror store networks.
- Quantization quality: Clara is worried about hallucinations in recipe outputs post-quantization. Add a short eval plan (prompt set + expected equivalence tests) to monitor quality regressions when moving to 4-bit.
- Observability: Jenna asked for token-level breakdowns per request and ability to tag requests with store_id. Need to confirm per-route retention and how to export traces to their Splunk instance.
- Cold-starts: edge nodes may be turned off overnight. Discussed a warm-start policy vs always-on for critical stores. Recommend canary with two warm replicas at hub.

Immediate action items (owner in parentheses):
- Prepare private-deploy checklist that includes: firewall egress IPs, offline install steps, model artifact transfer + checksum steps, KMS integration guide (Priya) — due 2025-09-24.
- Draft quantization eval plan with 200 prompt pair tests (Marcus + Clara) — coordinate by 2025-09-29.
- Estimate reserved capacity sizing for 3 hubs (SLA + burst buffer) and provide monthly cost projection (Sofia + Marcus) — draft by 2025-10-01.
- Create a short demo script for POS integration showing 120ms p50 on a 7B INT8 model with prefix caching enabled (Priya) — demo slot 2025-10-07.
- Open JIRA SE-4829 for air-gap packaging work and assign to infra team (Marcus).

Design options to discuss in follow-up:
A) Hybrid private: control plane in Redwood hosted, model execution on customer edge GPUs. Pro: faster iteration and easier rollouts. Con: customer firewall rules and egress IP mgmt.
B) Fully private: control plane and model execution in customer VPC (managed by Redwood OVA/terraform). Pro: max data control. Con: longer onboarding and ops handoff requirements.
C) Local inference+hosted-fallback: local nodes handle common prompts; heavy generative or long-context fall back to Redwood hosted (encrypted in transit). Pro: lower infra footprint on-site. Con: must solve PII routing rules and opt-in for fallback.

Risk/concerns to flag:
- KMS compatibility: they prefer Azure Key Vault; ensure we have tested HSM-backed keys in that flow.
- Compliance: Nightfall will want a SOC2 timetable; provide documentation of our private offering audit controls.
- Cost sensitivity to model size: moving to 13B will double infra cost — need to surface tradeoffs clearly in the cost proposal.

Notes for follow-up call agenda (tentative):
- Walk through private-deploy checklist + network diagram and required firewall rules. (15 min)
- Quantization eval plan + sample results from our small internal run. (20 min)
- Cost vs performance tradeoffs: 7B INT8 vs 13B INT8/FP16 and reserved capacity sizing. (20 min)
- On-prem installer timeline and responsibilities for air-gapped site. (15 min)

Loose transcript fragments captured in my notes:
- Jenna: "We need a setup that won't get in the way of a busy shift — if it adds latency our bartenders will hate it."
- Malik: "Firewalls are locked down; if you require incoming connections it's a non-starter."
- Clara: "Quantization is ok if we have a fast way to flag unexpected changes in output—need daily drift alerts."

References / tickets mentioned on call:
- SE-4829 (air-gap packaging)
- Internal PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra-private-deploy/PR-214
- Slack thread: #se-nightfall-onboarding (contains network diagrams)

Quick next steps (for me):
- Assemble the checklist doc + network diagram template, attach egress IPs placeholder for customer firewall team.
- Spin up a quick INT8 7B run with a 30-prompt recipe set to capture baseline latency and hallucination rate (goal: <8% unacceptable outputs).

Quick capture of possible prompts to include in eval suite (short list):
- "Suggest a 4-ingredient hazy IPA recipe using only 'Pale Malt', 'Vienna Malt', 'Citra', 'Mosaic', target OG 1.055"
- "Create a sprint cask seasonal porter recipe that ramps bitterness to 40 IBU and uses lactose. Explain substitution if lactose unavailable."
- "Given inventory: 20kg Pale, 3kg Munich, 2kg Chocolate, hops: Citra x1kg, Mosaic x500g; give 5 recipe variations for 20 L batch."

Status: call notes drafted, stakeholders aligned to follow-up meeting 2025-09-30 (tentative).

Notes end.
